Text: In Java, the compiler translates lambda expressions using the {{c1::invokedynamic}} bytecode instruction and dynamic bootstrap methods rather than traditional anonymous inner classes.
Extra: This runtime generation approach eliminates compile-time static class file generation overhead and JRE class loading footprint.

Text: Local variables captured by a lambda expression must be {{c1::final}} or {{c2::effectively final}} because local variables reside on the {{c3::stack}} while the lambda instance resides on the {{c4::heap}}.
Extra: Enforcing this prevents values from going out of sync when the stack frame is popped.

Text: For an unbound instance method reference like String::length, the first parameter of the functional interface is treated as the {{c1::receiver object}} (on which the method is called).
A lambda expression implementing a standard functional interface cannot throw {{c1::checked exceptions}} unless the interface method explicitly declares them.
Extra: Wrapping in try-catch or custom interfaces handles exceptions.

Text: Unlike anonymous inner classes, lambda expressions do not introduce a new scope; therefore, the {{c1::this}} keyword inside a lambda refers to the {{c2::enclosing class instance}}.
Extra: Lexical scoping rules apply inside lambdas.

Text: A functional interface is defined as an interface that has exactly {{c1::one}} abstract method, excluding any abstract methods overridden from {{c2::java.lang.Object}}.
Extra: Object overrides like equals() or toString() are ignored in the count.

Text: @FunctionalInterface is a(n) {{c1::optional}} annotation that ensures compile-time check that the interface contains exactly one abstract method.
Extra: Omitting it does not prevent the interface from being used as a functional interface target.

Text: In a bound instance method reference like prefix::startsWith, the receiver instance is resolved at {{c1::compile-time}}.
Extra: It is bound to that specific reference.

Text: If a local variable captured by a lambda is reassigned anywhere in the enclosing method, it is no longer {{c1::effectively final}}, causing a compile-time error.
Extra: The JLS prevents compilation when reassignment is detected.

Text: Under the hood, lambda expressions are compiled into private methods in the host class and instantiated at runtime using {{c1::LambdaMetafactory}}.
Extra: The dynamic class generated implements the target interface.

Text: An unmodifiable collection will throw {{c1::UnsupportedOperationException}} at runtime if you call mutating lambda-based methods like removeIf().
Extra: Methods like List.of() create unmodifiable collections.

Text: A classic bug when comparing integer values in a custom Comparator is using {{c1::subtraction}}, which can result in {{c2::integer overflow}}.
A method reference of the form ClassName::new is called a {{c1::constructor reference}}.
Extra: It maps to a constructor depending on the target parameters.
